design_rules.primary_subject: Choose the dominant topic from repeated channel and content evidence; allow unknown when evidence is insufficient.
design_rules.orthogonal_facets: Purpose, format, source, and account entity do not compete for topic slots.
design_rules.mixed_channels: Allow multiple calibrated topic paths; do not force a single topic when evidence is genuinely mixed.
design_rules.evidence: Every assigned node must cite current snapshot evidence and its source lineage.
design_rules.legacy_projection: The v1 adapter is lossy compatibility output and must never become v2 training truth.

topic.definition: What the channel is repeatedly about, independent of presentation format or communicative purpose.

nodes.definition: Cosmetics, skin, hair, grooming, and appearance-care subject matter.

Skin-care routines, products, and non-clinical skin education.
Clothing, footwear, accessories, and personal style subject matter.
Parenting practices, family life, pregnancy, babies, and children.

Homes, interiors, gardening, household equipment, and domestic improvement.

screen recordings without personal-life subject matter

purpose_genre.definition: Why or in what communicative genre the content is presented, independent of subject matter.

nodes.definition: Content intended to teach a repeatable process or skill.
Content intended to evaluate or compare products, services, places, or media.
Content intended to report timely events or developments.
Content intended to interpret, critique, or argue a viewpoint.
Content structured primarily as a narrative or recounted experience.
Content intended to document routine personal life over time.
excludes: any topic filmed as a vlog

nodes.definition: Content intended primarily to entertain through performance, humor, spectacle, or play.
Content intended to help viewers change habits, mindset, productivity, or personal capability.

format.definition: The observable delivery form of the content, independent of topic and purpose.

nodes.definition: Platform-designated or structurally short video content.
excludes: short excerpts misclassified as channel topic

nodes.definition: On-demand video outside the short-form and live formats.
Content broadcast live or preserved as a completed live replay.
Episode-based content led primarily by spoken audio or conversation.
Video whose primary visual surface is a captured screen or application interface.
excludes: software as topic without screen capture

nodes.definition: A person-centered portrait-oriented clip as an observable visual form.
Video primarily assembled from still photographs or image sequences.

source.definition: The provenance and production source of the published content, not the legal identity of the account owner.

nodes.definition: Content presented as original work by the publishing creator or team.
Content produced under an editorial, institutional, or professional publishing operation.
Content assembled primarily from user-generated material originating elsewhere.
Content republished from another source with an asserted license or distribution role.
Content provenance cannot be established from the available evidence.

entity.definition: The type of account or creator entity represented by the channel, separate from gender and content source.

nodes.definition: The channel is publicly represented as one identifiable creator.
excludes: unknown ownership inferred from a name

nodes.definition: The channel is publicly represented by multiple recurring creators.
excludes: organization staff with no creator identity

nodes.definition: The channel represents a company, institution, publisher, or brand rather than one creator.
The account entity type cannot be established from available public evidence.
